title: In Defense of Core-set: A Density-aware Core-set Selection for Active Learning

problem.claim: Active learning must select informative labeled samples from unlabeled data while handling redundant or highly similar samples.

gap.claim: Although core-set selection provides diversity, it performs poorly compared with uncertainty-based sampling.

contributions.claim: The work proposes density-aware core-set selection (DACS), which estimates unlabeled-sample density and selects diverse samples mainly from sparse regions.
The work introduces a locality-sensitive-hashing-based density approximation to reduce density-estimation computational bottlenecks.
The work presents a combination method that combines existing methods with DACS.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that DACS demonstrates efficacy in classification and regression tasks.
The authors report that DACS achieves state-of-the-art performance in a practical scenario.
The authors report that the combination method is simple and effective and that existing methods can benefit from being combined with DACS.

narrative_sequence.summary: Active learning constructs labeled datasets by selecting informative samples, and diversity-based sampling is important when samples are redundant or similar.
Core-set selection uses sample distances to select diverse samples, but performs worse than uncertainty-based selection.
Feature-space analysis indicates that locally sparse regions tend to contain more informative samples than dense regions.
DACS incorporates density awareness into core-set selection, and locality-sensitive hashing approximates density estimation.
The authors report results across classification and regression, state-of-the-art performance in a practical scenario, and benefits from combining existing methods with DACS.

source_observation.claim: Locally sparse feature-space regions tend to contain more informative samples than dense regions.

interpretation.claim: Sample density can provide a useful signal for prioritizing informative data points in active learning.

application.claim: When designing diversity-based active-learning selection, consider weighting or prioritizing samples from sparse regions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that sparse-region prioritization is appropriate for every dataset, model, or task.

unknowns: Datasets, metrics, baselines, and quantitative result values are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the density estimator or locality-sensitive hashing implementation in detail.
The practical scenario and architecture-dependence conditions are not specified.
